tool.name: FAIRe2NCBI: BioSample
tool.description: make an NCBI BioSample table from a FAIRe workbook
tool.command: set -o pipefail; @LINK_INPUT@ python '$__tool_directory__/faire2ncbi_galaxy.py' biosample --input_file input.xlsx #if str($bioproject).strip(): --bioproject '$bioproject' #end if @ORGANISM@ --mandatory_fill '$mandatory_fill' --associated '$associated' #if str($duplicates_column).strip(): --duplicates_column '$duplicates_column' #end if #if not $advanced.convert_dates: --no_date_conversion #end if #if not $advanced.mixs_units: --no_mixs_units #end if --sample_title '$advanced.title.sample_title' #if $advanced.title.sample_title == 'custom': --title_columns '$advanced.title.title_columns' #end if --extra_columns '$advanced.extra.extra_columns' #if $advanced.extra.extra_columns == 'except': --exclude_columns '$advanced.extra.exclude_columns' #end if --output '$biosample_table' --config_out '$config' < /dev/null | tee '$log'

param.name: bioproject
param.label: BioProject accession
param.help: The BioProject the samples belong to, for example PRJNA123456. Leave empty to link the BioProject later in the NCBI Submission Portal.

validator.message: Enter a BioProject accession such as PRJNA123456

param.name: mandatory_fill
param.label: Empty mandatory fields
param.help: What to do when a mandatory BioSample field (organism, collection date, depth, env_broad_scale, env_local_scale, env_medium, geo_loc_name, latitude and longitude) is empty for a sample. NCBI rejects empty mandatory fields. The terms are the INSDC missing-value terms.

param.name: associated
param.label: Samples to include
param.help: associatedSequences in experimentRunMetadata holds the NCBI links of runs already submitted. A cell holding NA or N/A counts as filled.
param.option: Only samples with no associatedSequences on any of their runs (new samples)

param.name: duplicates_column
param.label: Field that tells apart samples with identical attributes
param.help: NCBI will not register samples whose attributes are all the same apart from sample_name, sample_title and description, such as field replicates. If that happens, the tool adds this sampleMetadata field, for example replicate_number or extract_id. Leave empty to stop and list such samples.

param.name: convert_dates
param.label: Convert eventDate values for NCBI
param.help: NCBI needs collection times in UTC. With this on, a time zone offset is converted (2021-09-14T11:00+08:00 becomes 2021-09-14T03:00Z) and Excel date cells are written as ISO dates. With it off, values are passed unchanged.

param.name: mixs_units
param.label: Add MIxS preferred units
param.help: Numeric fields with a matching _unit field (for example temp_unit) always get that unit. With this on, other numeric fields get the MIxS preferred unit, for example 'degree Celsius' for temp. With it off, they are left as plain numbers.

param.name: sample_title
param.label: sample_title
param.help: A short title NCBI shows on the public BioSample page.

param.name: title_columns
param.label: BioSample columns to join
param.help: Comma-separated BioSample column names, for example sample_name,geo_loc_name,depth. The leading * of mandatory columns is optional.

validator.message: Use column names separated by commas

param.name: extra_columns
param.label: Other sampleMetadata fields
param.help: sampleMetadata fields that are not BioSample attributes can be added as extra columns, which NCBI keeps as custom attributes. Fields that are empty for every sample are never added.

param.name: exclude_columns
param.label: Fields to leave out
param.help: Comma-separated sampleMetadata field names, for example samp_collect_notes,dna_store_loc

validator.message: Use field names separated by commas

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool turns the **sampleMetadata** sheet of a FAIRe workbook into a BioSample table for the NCBI Submission Portal, using NCBI's *MIMARKS: survey, water* package (version 6.0). Upload the table on the *Attributes* tab of a BioSample or SRA submission at https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov
FAIRe2NCBI normally asks you questions as it runs. In Galaxy, the tool answers them from the form. It also writes a **config** file holding those answers, so that the same run can be repeated outside Galaxy.
-----
**Inputs**
- **A FAIRe workbook** (.xlsx). The samples come from sampleMetadata. experimentRunMetadata is used only to find samples that have already been submitted (associatedSequences). - **The BioProject accession** (optional). - **The organism** to use for samples that have none. NCBI needs an organism, for example *marine metagenome*, and FAIRe has no organism field.
**Outputs**
- **BioSample table**: NCBI's template header (11 comment lines), followed by one row for each sample. - **config**: the answers given to FAIRe2NCBI, as YAML. - **log**: a record of what FAIRe2NCBI and the tool did.
-----
**What the tool changes before conversion**
- eventDate values with a time zone offset are converted to UTC, as NCBI asks. - Empty organism values are filled with the organism you chose. - If you choose a missing-value term, empty mandatory fields are filled with it. If you do not, the tool stops and lists them. - Rows without a samp_name are ignored. - Whole numbers stay whole (14, not 14.0), and lat_lon keeps the decimal places of decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude. (FAIRe2NCBI on its own rounds them to 3 places, which is about 100 m.)
**Checks**
- NCBI will not register samples whose attributes are all the same apart from sample_name, sample_title and description, which is common for field replicates. To avoid this, give a field that tells them apart, such as replicate_number. The check runs before the other sampleMetadata fields are added, so it can report samples that those fields would have told apart. - Collection dates that NCBI may not be able to read (for example 7/6/19) are listed in the log as warnings.
